program: Eviction Defense Collaborative / Tenant Right to Counsel full-scope legal defense
decisionUnit: An additional tenant household retaining the right to occupy its home because full-scope legal representation was provided instead of less intensive assistance

bottomLine.interpretation: San Francisco budgeted $315,000 for a fully loaded Tenant Right to Counsel legal-defense team with a 50-case deliverable, or $6,300 per historical full-scope case. Applying a judgmental 5-point retained-possession effect gives a conditional estimate of $126,000 per additional household retaining possession. The randomized evidence conflicts by court and comparison service, so a null effect remains plausible and the true upper bound is not finite.

inputs.label: Illustrative gift
inputs.basis: Donor scenario, not published current funding room

inputs.label: City fully loaded legal-defense team cost
inputs.basis: MOHCD FY2023–24 Tenant Right to Counsel presentation: one attorney, support and supervision fractions, $660 litigation expense per client, and 15% overhead. Public budget context, not EDC marginal cost.
inputs.confidence: high for published budget; not marginal

inputs.label: City full-scope team case deliverable
inputs.basis: MOHCD states that new attorneys require ramp-up time to achieve a deliverable goal of 50 cases. The presentation does not define case complexity, completion, or follow-up.
inputs.confidence: high for published target; moderate as denominator

inputs.label: Historical public cost per full-scope case
inputs.basis: $315,000 fully loaded team cost divided by the 50-case deliverable. This is a TRC-wide historical budget ratio, not an EDC invoice, causal price, or current marginal offer.

inputs.label: NYC randomized adverse-judgment reduction
inputs.basis: Final judgments were entered against 22% of represented tenants and 51% of unrepresented tenants in an older New York City randomized experiment. Judgment is not the same as retained possession, and the setting differs sharply from current San Francisco.
inputs.confidence: high for study; very indirect for EDC

inputs.label: SF descriptive stayed-home difference
inputs.basis: MOHCD reported 63% of full-scope clients stayed in their homes versus 45% receiving limited-scope assistance at settlement conference. This was not reported as randomized or adjusted and is not an EDC effect.

inputs.label: MFI estimate of absolute retained-possession effect
inputs.basis: Judgmental transfer set well below the NYC randomized 29-point adverse-judgment effect and the SF unadjusted 18-point comparison because the Massachusetts Housing Court experiment found no retained-possession gain from full versus limited assistance. The numeric range is conditional on a positive effect; null or harm remains outside it.

formula.rangeMethod: Fixed FY2023–24 public team-cost ratio with favorable, midpoint, and small-positive effect scenarios
formula.denominatorBoundary: The 50 cases are a city staffing deliverable, not a published count of completed, unique, EDC-only cases. Retaining the right to occupy is narrower than avoiding homelessness and does not specify duration.

nullEffectBoundary: The conditional range does not include zero or harm. Full representation did not outperform limited assistance on retained possession in the Massachusetts Housing Court experiment. If San Francisco's limited-scope and referral system already captures the marginal benefit, if vulnerability scoring selects harder cases, or if a gift displaces public funding, additional retained-possession outcomes may approach zero or become negative and cost per additional outcome has no finite upper bound.

fundingRoom.boundary: The $100,000 scenario is illustrative. The city budget and eight reported attorney vacancies show scale and an implementation constraint, but not an EDC philanthropic gap, private-dollar additionality, or a current case price.
fundingRoom.requiredNext: Obtain EDC's dated $100K, $1M, and $10M expansion plans; public reimbursement and displacement rules; current vacancies and ramp time; EDC-only full-scope case counts; assignment rules; and linked 3-, 6-, 12-, and 24-month housing outcomes.

excludedBenefits: The city's 63% versus 45% stayed-home comparison as a causal effect
